newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Coal & Allied coal strike to end - union.
newsitem.headline: Coal & Allied coal strike to end - union.

text.p: Union officials will recommend to workers at Coal & Allied Ltd's strike-bound Hunter Valley Number One mine north of Sydney that they vote on Tuesday morning to end the strike from midnight, union officials said.

Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU) official Mick Kelly told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio the union had agreed to recommend the return to work after talks with Coal and Allied late on Monday.
The union had also agreed to provide labour to load a coal train at 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT) on Tuesday if members vote to return to work at an early morning meeting, Kelly said.
The strike began on June 11 and was initially expected to last two weeks, but has dragged on and had threatened to widen to port and transport workers.
Coal and Allied has estimated the strike would cost it A$1 million a day in lost revenue.
Kelly said the union had been prepared to take action to "bring about serious negotiations."
"We believe that's what has been achieved. It remains to be seen just how genuine the company is, but I'm taking them at their word," Kelly said.
Mine manager Allan Davies said the end of the strike was a win for the company.
"What it does is provide a basis for us to get on and negotiate the agreement which is always what I've wanted to do," Davies told ABC radio.
"The union has decided to recommend that their members come back to work and that's great, that's terrific, and I'm pleased to see that they've seen sense."
Coal and Allied increased its average pay rise on offer to the 412 striking workers to A$170 a week from A$150 a week.
Coal and Alied is 71 percent owned by Anglo-Australian mining house Rio Tinto Ltd. The shipment was due to be delivered to a Korean customer.
Coal and Allied's attempt to negotiate more flexible enterprise bargains, the main reason for the strike, is seen as a key battle in the industry's drive to improve profitability.
Coal and Allied closed unchanged at A$9.40 on Monday.
